text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000199 bills 99215 well above expectation across every complexity level, but the few charts returned support the billed level, so the pattern cannot yet be attributed to upcoding or to a sicker panel.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The by-complexity table shows this provider's 99215 share running well above the all-provider share in every stratum, from 0-condition to 5+-condition patients. That points to a provider-wide coding tendency rather than one explained only by sicker patients, although the panel does include many genuinely multimorbid patients (for example C0097998 and C0098277), for whom high-level visits are plausible. The concern is the low-complexity 99215s in the sample: C0097652 (acute URI, no chronic conditions), C0098352 (an 18-year-old with back pain) and C0098496 (rash only) are visits where a high-complexity level is hard to explain from the claim alone. The records review cuts the other way but is too thin to judge: all 4 documented 99215 claims were supported at high MDM, the single below-billed note was a 99214 (C0098634), and no moderate-plus data-reviewed notes lacked a lab or test line. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims, since those would most directly separate upcoding from legitimate complexity, and then check whether the provider's heavy 99214 volume shows the same pattern."}
